When a customer emails asking for a refund, find their order and the amount from the email. Refunds under $50 are approved on their own. Anything larger goes to a support lead in Slack with the order details, and they approve or decline it. An approved refund is paid back in Stripe and the customer gets a reply saying so. If the order cannot be found or Stripe refuses the refund, tell the support lead in Slack and pay nothing until they decide.

When an employee submits an expense in Slack with a photo of the receipt, check that it has an amount, a date and a category. Expenses under $100 are approved on their own. Larger ones go to the employee's manager, and anything over $1,000 also needs someone in finance. Approved expenses are added to the reimbursement sheet. If the receipt is missing or unreadable, ask the employee to send it again before anyone reviews it.

When a supplier emails an invoice, read the supplier, the amount and the due date. An invoice from a known supplier that matches an open purchase order is approved on its own. Every other invoice goes to a finance manager in Slack, who approves it, rejects it or asks the supplier a question. Approved invoices are recorded in QuickBooks to be paid before the due date. If an invoice looks like one already received, hold it and tell the finance manager.

Every Monday at 9am, gather last week's support tickets: how many came in, how many were solved, the slowest replies and the most common topics. Write a short summary and send it to the support lead in Slack to check. Once they approve it, post it in the support team's channel. If the ticket system cannot be reached, tell the support lead and try again an hour later.

When someone asks for time off in Slack, record the dates and the reason. Their manager approves or declines it in Slack. Approved time off goes on the team calendar and the person gets a confirmation. Requests for more than ten working days also need someone in HR. If the manager has not answered within two working days, remind them, and after four tell HR.

When HR emails that a new hire signed their offer, ask the hiring manager in Slack which team and tools the person needs. Once they answer, create the person's work account in Google Workspace, add them to the team's Slack channels and email them their first-day details. If an account with that name already exists, stop and ask the hiring manager before creating anything.

In internal/process/text_summary_flow.go, add a human approval before the summary is saved. Add a Step AwaitSummaryApproval between GenerateSummary and SaveSummaryResult: route the GenerateSummary Generated branch to it and leave its other branches unchanged. Its WaitFor sets summary-status to "awaiting-approval", which Display shows while the run waits, and waits for one message on a new Channel SummaryApprovals; its Execute passes the generated result on to SaveSummaryResult. Add an Action RPC ApproveSummary with no input, label "Approve summary", condition summary-status == "awaiting-approval" and permission summary.approve; it rechecks that status and publishes to SummaryApprovals directly in the RPC method. Follow AGENTS.md and "Answer a waiting Step" in /opt/superverse/dex-skills/dex-app-builder/references/fdg-authoring.md. Change nothing else. Show these requirements with confirm_requirements before you change any file, then build them. Run go build ./... and make check-fdg-v2, then commit and push to the default branch with commit_and_push.

Implement a simple approval-based GreetingFlow in this new template project. Use the template Go backend and toolchain; keep its Dex SDK unless a newer stable release is needed. Replace the reference TextSummaryFlow, its summary-model connection, text-summary endpoints and form with the concrete Go type GreetingFlow, using SDK default Flow and Step identities without naming overrides. Its durable steps must validate a trimmed nonempty name, wait for the real approval Channel, and complete with the exact result "Hello, <name>!". Replace the summary form with a real application HTTP start/approve/read path and UI controls named Automation request, Start process and Approve, plus a result element with test ID result. Change the app main heading to exactly "Local Native Greeting". Register every retained primitive and update dex-app.yaml, the Flow Definition artifacts, registry/client wiring and documentation. Use Dex as the durable owner; add no database, connectors or mock dependencies. Run the template real checks and strict FDG 2.0 validation, commit all application changes and push the accepted default branch. Complete implementation directly; the requested Flow and existing template UI are already authorized.

Build a simple English-language release newsletter application. A public page lets visitors subscribe with their email address and stores each subscriber once. An administrator starts a newsletter in Studio Runs. It reads published releases from the last seven days in the superdurable GitHub organization repositories dex, dex-skills, and dex-connectors-library, excluding drafts and prereleases. Use OpenAI to produce a concise email draft with links to the source releases. The run then waits for administrator review in Studio Inbox. The administrator can approve it or request revision with written feedback; a revised draft must wait for approval again. After approval, send the approved draft through Gmail separately to every subscriber present when sending begins, without exposing the recipient list. Show the draft, review status, and delivery outcome in the run. An uncertain email delivery must be clearly reported and must not be automatically sent again. Keep the public UI simple. No Slack, scheduled sending, unsubscribe, double opt-in, or separate administrator UI is needed. Implement the application, verify its source, and commit and push it. I will configure credentials and validate real execution afterward.
Inspect the existing application template. Run its source checks and report readiness. Preserve TextSummaryFlow, its summary form and its API; use Studio Runs for process management.
